children: 在战争日记中描述他如何克服对死亡的恐惧时，阿菲诺格诺夫表达了一个担忧：他的日记能幸存吗？“你，我未来的偶然读者，你会在哪里找到这个笔记本？当你背着麻袋走在这个伟大国家的公路上时，你会停下来从地上捡起这本落满灰尘的小书，还是会像其他人一样，因旅途劳顿而踩在上面继续前行？”

While describing in his war diary how he mastered his fear of death, Afinogenov voiced one worry: Would his diary survive? “You, my future accidental reader, where will you find this notebook? As you wander the highways of this great country, with a sack on your shoulders, will you stop to pick up this dust-covered little book from the ground, or will you, like others, tread on it, tired from the long journey, and keep walking?”
对于阿菲诺格诺夫这个对自己作为苏联剧作家的平反程度仍不确定的人来说，这些问题指涉的不止是他的日记。决定性的问题是，他的整个生命将如何被铭记。他是否会被后世承认是一个真正的布尔什维克，还是苏联人民会践踏他在斯大林清洗中被丢弃、躺在尘土中的剧作？

For Afinogenov, who remained uncertain about the extent of his rehabilitation as a Soviet playwright, these questions referred to more than his diary. The decisive question was how his life as a whole would be remembered. Would he be recognized by posterity as a genuine Bolshevik, or would the Soviet people trample his plays, which had been discarded in the Stalinist purges, underfoot as they lay in the dust?
阿菲诺格诺夫始终关注死亡以及自己死后在苏联集体记忆中的存在，与共产党人的自我实现是一致的，这种自我实现随着共产党人进入历史的万神殿而达到顶峰。一个共产党人的生理寿命是短暂且次要的，相比之下，他作为一个历史主体的生命可以延续到死后很久，但这取决于在历史上更先进的后代是否赋予他一种“历史性”的存在。

Afinogenov’s insistent orientation toward his death and afterlife in Soviet collective memory was consistent with Communist self-realization, which reached its highest point with the Communist entering the pantheon of history. A Communist’s biological life span was brief and inferior compared with his life as a historical subject, which could extend long after his death, but which depended on whether historically more advanced posterity granted him a “historical” existence.

在他去世后的几年里，朋友和同事们的悼词证明了阿菲诺格诺夫是一个与历史对话的共产党人。在为阿菲诺格诺夫逝世三周年准备的回忆录中，鲍里斯·帕斯捷尔纳克（Boris Pasternak）对他进行了描述，其措辞与阿菲诺格诺夫试图为自己保留的青春永驻的模板惊人地相似：“在他身上……有一种理想的气质。他高大苗条，动作优雅；高昂的头颅带有古典式规整的特征，在某种程度上与他纯洁与力量统一的内在性格之美相呼应。他的才华也是如此：它散发出青春的清新，是一种轻盈、透明的古典风貌。”帕斯捷尔纳克没有直接提到历史，但在将阿菲诺格诺夫塑造成古典英雄时，他将阿菲诺格诺夫与斯大林体制的自我呈现——即作为一个处于人类发展巅峰的新古典主义时代——联系在了一起。鲍里斯·伊格里茨基（Boris Igritsky）在1946年写道，他更直接地探讨了阿菲诺格诺夫生活的历史属性。这位剧作家曾“寻找过许多东西，……做了很多实验……但他从未回避或躲避生活，从未躲避他的时代、它的风暴和暴雨、它的激情及其困难。他与党和人民共同成长，他勇敢地向前、向前迈进。”像这样“随党勇敢前进”的意象是标准的苏联赞美公式，也同样被用于纪念其他去世的作家。但置于阿菲诺格诺夫私人写作的背景下，这些修辞陈词滥调揭示了苏联意识形态语言与共产党人主体经验之间强烈的意义转移。

Eulogies by friends and colleagues in the years after his death vindicated Afinogenov as a Communist who communed with history. In a memoir prepared for the third anniversary of Afinogenov’s death, Boris Pasternak described him in terms uncannily similar to the mold of youthful immortality that Afinogenov had sought to preserve for himself: “There was something ideal . . . about him. He was tall and slender, and he moved gracefully; his highly held head had features of classical regularity, somehow corresponding to the beauty of his inner character, which united purity and strength. Such was also his talent: it exuded the freshness of youth, a light, transparent, classical mold.” Pasternak did not directly refer to history, but in casting Afinogenov as a classical hero he aligned him with the Stalinist system’s self-representation as a neoclassical age standing at the apogee of developed humanity. Writing in 1946, Boris Igritsky addressed the historical quality of Afinogenov’s life more directly. The playwright had “searched for many things, . . . experimented a lot . . . but he never shunned or hid from life, from his epoch, its storms and tempests, its passions, and its difficulties. He grew with the party and the people, he boldly marched forward, forward.” Images like this one, of “boldly marching forward with the party,” were standard Soviet laudatory formulas and were equally applied to honor other dead writers. But set against the background of Afinogenov’s intimate writings these rhetorical clichés disclose an intense transfer of meaning between Soviet ideological language and the Communist’s subjective experience.

1946年10月29日，阿菲诺格诺夫逝世五周年之际，莫斯科作家之家举行了一场“追思晚会”。多位作家向这位已故同事致敬；主持会议的是弗谢沃洛德·维什涅夫斯基（Vsevolod Vishnevsky），正是这位维什涅夫斯基在1937年4月那次命中注定的会议上对阿菲诺格诺夫提出了公开指责。当晚最引人注目的发言来自作家维克托·芬克（Viktor Fink）。他研究过阿菲诺格诺夫的日记，想向听众分享他对这份文件的印象：

摆在你面前的是一大叠厚厚的纸，一个人在其中只与自己生活在一起，并将灵魂倾注于此。它展现了一个全新的、隐藏的世界，周围的人看不见，一套无人知晓的想法和行为……[这些日记]不仅呈现了有趣的传记和文学材料，它们还是研究当代进步人士的有趣材料：他写了什么，如何写的，以及他是如何生活的。在阅读数百页的过程中，我看到的无非是具有基本社会、文学和政治意义的主题。这是一个拥抱最高理想的人。这个人的全身心投入和精神纯洁让我充满了羡慕和欣喜。

On October 29, 1946, the fifth anniversary of Afinogenov’s death, an “evening of remembrance” took place at the Moscow House of Writers. A range of writers paid tribute to their late colleague; presiding over the meeting was Vsevolod Vishnevsky, the same Vishnevsky who had formulated the public accusation against Afinogenov at the fateful meeting of April 1937. The most remarkable speech of the evening came from the writer Viktor Fink. He had studied Afinogenov’s diary and wanted to share his impressions about the document with his audience:

Before you lies a voluminous stack of paper, in which a person lives just with himself and onto which he has poured his soul. It presents a new, hidden world, invisible to the people around him, a set of ideas and deeds that nobody has known about . . . [The diaries] do not just present interesting biographical and literary material, they are interesting material for the study of a progressive person of our time: what he wrote about and how he wrote, how he lived. In reading through hundreds of pages, I did not see anything but themes of fundamental social, literary, and political interest. This was a man who embraced the highest ideals. The wholehearted nature and spiritual purity of this person filled me with envy and delight.
考虑到这部日记的精神完整性，芬克接着说，他产生了一个想法。类比于能够恢复过去文明生命的考古学，“或许人文科学将进步到这样一种程度，即人们将学会如何根据一个人的著作来重构其道德和生理特征。”以这种方式，未来的科学家将能够“重构……阿菲诺格诺夫，一个外表英俊、身材高大、长着年轻希腊半神般圆润头颅的人；一个对生活的公正充满平静信心，并对自己的创造力充满信心的人。”

芬克所阐述的是尼古拉·费奥多罗夫（Nikolai Fedorov）复活哲学的字面应用。这位19世纪的哲学家相信个人著作构成了一个人的核心，他主张建立一种国家秩序来保存这些著作，直到科学进步使人能够从其文本的精神提取物中实现生理复活。芬克与费奥多罗夫以及几代俄罗斯知识分子都有一个共同的假设，即一个人的核心存在于其著作中。文本不仅是现实的反映，它还是意识的核心。对芬克而言，阿菲诺格诺夫的日记构成了一个充实、非凡生命的本质。

芬克说，日记的任何读者都会产生一种强烈的意识，即只有“伟大的人们和伟大的时代”才能孕育出阿菲诺格诺夫这样的人。他的言论揭示了那种赋予阿菲诺格诺夫生命的“历史意识”在他死后依然延续。就像阿菲诺格诺夫一样，芬克等人也在寻找能肯定社会主义社会现实的历史标志。现在，阿菲诺格诺夫通过他的早逝，成为了这样一个历史路标。他生命中不容置疑的完整性和美感，被幸存的同代人视为新社会主义人确实存在的证据。这种解读掩盖了阿菲诺格诺夫自己对他不完整性的感知。

In light of the spiritual integrity of this journal, Fink went on, a thought had occurred to him. In analogy to the science of archaeology, which was able to restore past civilizations to life, “perhaps the human sciences will advance to the point that people will learn how to reconstruct the moral and physical features of a person based on his writings.” In such fashion a future scientist would be able to “reconstruct . . . Afinogenov, a person who was physically handsome, tall, endowed with the round head of a young Greek demigod; a person who lived with a calm confidence in the justice of life, and confidence in his own creative powers.”

What Fink laid out was a literal application of Nikolai Fedorov’s philosophy of resurrection. Believing that personal writings formed the core of a person, the nineteenth-century philosopher had advocated a state order that would preserve these writings until scientific progress would make possible a person’s physical resurrection from the spiritual extract of his texts. Fink shared an assumption with Fedorov and generations of the Russian intelligentsia that the core of a person resided in his or her writings. A text was not simply a reflection of reality; it was the very heart of consciousness. For Fink, Afinogenov’s diary formed the essence of a fully lived, extraordinary life.

Any reader of the diary, Fink said, would take away a powerful sense that only “great people and a great epoch” could have given birth to someone like Afinogenov. His remark revealed that the historical consciousness that had animated Afinogenov’s life lived on after his death. Just like Afinogenov, Fink and others searched for historical markers that would affirm the reality of socialist society. Now Afinogenov, through his early death, had become one such historical road mark. The unassailable integrity and beauty of his life was seen by his surviving contemporaries as evidence that the new socialist man did in fact exist. It was an interpretation that belied Afinogenov’s own sense of his incompleteness.

在阿菲诺格诺夫逝世周年纪念日悼念他的人中，没有人提到他的家人：他的妻子和女儿后来怎么样了，或者他年迈的母亲是如何应对失去独子的痛苦的。阿菲诺格诺夫的日记在很大程度上也对他生活的这一面保持沉默。无论是日记作者还是纪念他的作家，都坚持关注历史。他们强调一个人的生活中他们认为具有历史价值的那些方面。尽管1937年阿菲诺格诺夫的日记带有内省和隐遁的基调，但它并不是他个人生活的记录。例如，他几乎没有提到他第二个女儿的出生。
那一年日记中深刻的个人特质，首先源于阿菲诺格诺夫认识到他的生命突然获得了历史意义：历史以斯大林清洗的形式直接穿透了他。他捕捉自己生命的戏剧，将其视为具有历史规模的戏剧。此外，剧作家的职业与他作为共产党人的生活密不可分，这种生活被对历史性存在的追求所定义。这种对历史意义的渴望解释了为什么阿菲诺格诺夫寻求在斗争、强制和破坏的时代最充分地实现他的生命。

None of those who eulogized Afinogenov at the anniversaries of his death mentioned his family: what had happened to his wife and daughters or how his aged mother had coped with the loss of her only son. Afinogenov’s diary, too, had been largely silent about this side of his life. Both the diarist and the writers who remembered him focused insistently on history. They stressed those aspects of a person’s life which they believed to carry historical value. Despite its introspective and reclusive tone, Afinogenov’s diary of 1937 was not a record of his personal life. For instance, he hardly mentioned the birth of his second daughter. The deeply personal quality of that year’s diary stems in the first place from Afinogenov’s recognition that his life had suddenly acquired historical meaning: history, in the form of Stalin’s purges, was passing directly through him. He seized on the drama of his own life as a drama of historical proportions. In addition, the vocation of playwright was inextricably connected to his life as a Communist, a life defined by a striving for a historical existence. This craving for historical significance explains why Afinogenov sought to realize his life to the fullest in a time of utmost struggle, coercion, and destruction.

en:
Afinogenov wrote Fear in 1930 against the background of the trial
of the Industrial party, which also figures in the diary of Zinaida
Denis’evskaia. He wanted to explore the conflicted inner world of the
bourgeois specialists and thus explain how they could commit the
monstrous deeds of which they were accused. See Julie A. Cassiday,
The Enemy on Trial: Early Soviet Courts on Stage and Screen (DeKalb:
Northern Illinois University Press, 2000), 176–181.

the last lines of the fourth letter did Kirshon embark on self-criti-

en:
Karaganov, Zhizn’ dramaturga, 515. On the fifth anniversary of
Afinogenov’s death the writer Boris Gorbatov remarked: “He died a
very good death. . . . There is something symbolic about this death.
It is the death of a Bolshevik, a Communist, such as we all knew
Afinogenov.” RGALI, f. 1614, op. 1, ed. 255, l. 13. On Soviet Communist
notions of death, see Halfin, Terror in My Soul.

这种作为历史主体的自我构想促使尼古拉·布哈林写了一封《致未来一代党的领导人》的信。他在被捕前夕创作了这封信，并敦促他的妻子记熟，以便在死后能流传下去。布哈林在审判中将其最后的申辩投向“世界历史”，视其为“世界法庭”。见安娜·拉里娜（Anna Larina）著，《我不能忘记：尼古拉·布哈林遗孀回忆录》（纽约：诺顿出版社，1993年），第343–345页；《大清洗审判》，罗伯特·塔克和斯蒂芬·科恩编（纽约：格罗斯特与邓拉普出版社，1965年），第667页。
en:
This self-conception as a historical subject prompted Nikolai Bu-
kharin to write a letter “To a Future Generation of Party Leaders.” He
composed it on the eve of his arrest and urged his wife to learn it by
heart so that its message would survive beyond his death. Bukharin
addressed his last plea at his trial to “world history” as a “world court
of judgment.” See Anna Larina, This I Cannot Forget: The Memoirs of
Nikolai Bukharin’s Widow (New York: Norton, 1993), 343–345; The Great
Purge Trial, ed. Robert Tucker and Stephen Cohen (New York: Grosset
& Dunlap, 1965), 667.

zh: 阿菲诺格诺夫的一生不断被重写。1977年苏联版的日记删减了他1937年的个人主义情绪，并将其描绘成一位坚定的共产党员，但最近的一份出版物恰恰优先考虑了这些部分，并将其描绘成一个抵抗斯大林主义政权的主体。见阿菲诺格诺夫著，《选集》，第2卷；同前著，《1937年日记》。
en:
Afinogenov’s life keeps being rewritten. The 1977 Soviet edition of his
diary censored his individualist moods of 1937 and portrayed him as a
steadfast Communist, but a more recent publication privileges pre-
cisely these sections and casts him as a subject who resisted the Sta-
linist regime. Afinogenov, Izbrannoe, t. 2; idem, “Dnevnik 1937 goda.”
